items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia to set up joint working group to boost rural development
items.summary: BALI: Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish a joint working group (JWG) to strengthen cooperation in rural development, including through the exchange of best practices in village management in both countries. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is currently on a working visit to Indonesia, said Malaysia could benefit from Indonesia's experience specifically its more structured village rating system to improve data collection and the effectiveness of rural development programme implementation. This, he said, would assist the government in planning development programmes more effectively.

items.title: 'He helped anyone in need': A. Samad Said remembered for generosity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Beyond his towering literary legacy, the late National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr A. Samad Said is remembered for his generosity in helping underprivileged youths pursue their education. National Laureate Datuk Dr Zurinah Hassan said she was among those touched by his kindness, recalling how he agreed to act as guarantor for her Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) student loan when she studied at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM). Zurinah said his generosity extended to many others in need, regardless of their background.

items.title: Arthur: Asean's mineral wealth must benefit its people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asean must ensure its mineral wealth benefits its people, drives innovation and protects the environment as global competition for critical minerals intensifies. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the region's mineral resources and growing economy had attracted global attention. He was speaking at the gala dinner for the 11th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals and the Asean Minerals Investment Forum (AMVest) in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.

items.title: Trump could gain up to US$15mil from Nvidia shares after Huang's return: FT
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The spectacular rebound in Nvidia's share price following Jensen Huang's return as chief executive could have added as much as US$15 million to US President Donald Trump's holdings in the stock on Monday, according to calculations by the Financial Times. News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring more than 30 per cent and added more than US$900 billion to the company's market value. According to the Financial Times, Trump may have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of Sept 30.

items.title: RTM to broadcast special 'Dialog Negara' episode featuring Anwar tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Radio Televisyen Malaysia will broadcast a special episode of the high-impact national discourse programme, "Dialog Negara", featuring Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as the main guest at 9pm tomorrow. According to the statement, the special episode opens up space for a deeper discussion regarding the considerations, challenges, and rationale behind major decisions made by the government in its efforts to strengthen national development and improve the people's well-being. "The discussion will focus on four main dimensions: Behind a Decision, Behind Reforms and Change, Behind the People's Hopes, and Behind Malaysia's Future," the statement said.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Tuesday, November 24, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1585003]] [[nid:1585002]] [[nid:1585001]] [[nid:1585000]] [[nid:1584999]] [[nid:1584998]] [[nid:1584997]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: WTS Capital's Q2 profit rises 18pct on revenue surge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: WTS Capital Bhd, formerly known as Systech Bhd, posted an 18 per cent increase in net profit to RM1.48 million in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM1.25 million a year earlier, driven by higher revenue. Revenue surged 188.5 per cent to RM48.03 million from RM16.64 million. For the six months ended Sept 30, 2026, WTS Capital's net profit rose to RM2.93 million from RM734,000 a year earlier, while revenue surged 530 per cent to RM200.07 million from RM31.76 million.

items.title: Penang fast-tracks water projects as demand set to rise
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang is accelerating major water projects, including desalination and inter-state water supply, as demand is projected to rise by 27.2 per cent to 1,100 million litres per day (MLD) by 2032. Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) chief executive officer Datuk K. Pathmanathan said demand stood at 865 MLD last year, with the projection based on feedback from the manufacturing sector, property developers and state development agencies. Under the Penang Water Supply Roadmap 2040, the Water Contingency Plan 2030 aims to increase treated water production by 602 MLD, build 4 water treatment plants in Seberang Perai and increase supply to the island.

items.title: IGP: Tony Pua may be summoned over leaked Pardons Board meeting minutes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have not ruled out summoning DAP leader Tony Pua to assist in investigations into the disclosure of minutes from a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. However, he said police had yet to receive any formal reports concerning the issue. Earlier, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail directed the police to mobilise all available resources to investigate the alleged disclosure of the meeting minutes.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 24, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Refugee registration tightened Only refugee registrations administered by the Immigration Department and Home Ministry will be recognised as valid under a new cabinet decision. Kindergarten age review The Education Ministry is considering allowing children aged three-plus to enrol in kindergartens following changes to Year One entry requirements. Highway proposals studied The Works Ministry is studying private sector proposals to build tolled highways aimed at easing congestion along the Federal Highway.

items.title: Anwar pays tribute to literary icon A. Samad Said
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has paid tribute to National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr A. Samad Said, describing him as a literary figure whose works and advocacy for the Malay language and justice would continue to inspire generations. In a social media post, Anwar said he received news of the writer's passing with sadness. Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, extended their condolences to Samad's family and prayed for strength for those mourning his passing.

items.title: Man found dead in Nibong Tebal was hit in the head
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Blunt force injuries to the head were the cause of death of an unidentified man whose body was discovered in Kampung Baru, Jalan Byram, yesterday. Seberang Prai Selatan police chief Superintendent Jay January Siowou said the cause of death was confirmed following a post-mortem examination conducted at Seberang Jaya Hospital today. He said police received a report regarding the discovery of the body at the Kampung Baru area along Jalan Byram yesterday.

items.title: Govt plans digital access to MyKad
items.summary: Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the ministry was also looking at integrating passports, birth and marriage certificates, and other personal documents into the MyGov Malaysia application. He said discussions involving GovTech, MyGov and MyDigital ID were held yesterday following a directive from the Prime Minister. Gobind said users could currently view their MyKad details digitally, but not display the card itself, unlike driving licences issued by the Road Transport Department.

items.title: Hadi claims non-Muslims turning to Pas over discomfort with DAP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang says the party is gaining support from non-Muslims who are uncomfortable with DAP, which he described as extreme. He said Pas was confident of defeating Pakatan Harapan in the 16th General Election (GE16), citing the results of recent state elections. It means even non-Muslims are no longer supporting DAP.

items.title: 'Sabah govt should set up special committee for resettlement of Kampung Pondo'
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government has been told to establish a special committee to oversee the proposed resettlement of Kampung Pondo residents on Gaya island off here. Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (Star) president Datuk Seri Jeffrey Kitingan said the proposed Pulau Gaya Resettlement and Residents' Welfare Committee should include representatives of the affected residents. "Sabah must safeguard its authority over immigration matters.

items.title: Arthur gives assurance on environmental safeguards in rare earth mining
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Environmental protection will remain a priority in rare earth mining, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup. He said Malaysia had published its export requirements before approving the supply of raw rare earth materials to France for research. Under the agreement, France will share its rare earth processing technology with Malaysia.

items.title: Greatech unit to acquire two industrial complexes in Penang for RM153mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Greatech Technology Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary, Greatech Integration (M) Sdn Bhd, has entered into two separate sale and purchase agreements with Penfabric Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of two industrial complexes in Phase 3 Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone, Bayan Lepas, Penang for a total consideration of RM153 million. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the acquisitions comprise the first industrial complex for RM63 million and the second for RM90 million. Greatech Technology said the proposed acquisition represents a strategic investment by the group in acquiring industrial properties strategically located within the Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone, Penang, which is an established industrial hub.

items.title: Jetour Malaysia assembles 10,000 vehicles, expand regional export footprint
items.summary: Its first overseas shipment comprised the Jetour Dashing, marking the start of its export operations from Malaysia. Jetour Malaysia chief executive officer Fu Yong said Malaysia was important to the company's long-term development in the Asia-Pacific region. "Malaysia is an important part of Jetour's long-term development in the Asia-Pacific region.

items.title: Macron's visit puts RM600mil heritage restoration in new light
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM600 million allocation to restore the Sultan Abdul Samad Building complex and Carcosa Seri Negara, which was previously questioned in Parliament, has taken on a different perspective following French President Emmanuel Macron's recent visit to Kuala Lumpur. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the public response to Macron's visit highlighted the value of investing in heritage conservation and preserving the capital's historical identity. "I remember the painful discussion in Parliament when the prime minister first announced that he would spend RM600 million to restore the Sultan Abdul Samad Building.

items.title: Sum Technology secures RM48mil data centre subcontract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sum Technology Bhd has secured a subcontract for a data centre project in Selangor with a provisional contract value of approximately RM48 million. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said its wholly owned subsidiary, Sum Technic Sdn Bhd, accepted the letter of award to provide mechanical, electrical, process utilities and firefighting subcontracting works. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia still weighing whether to export rare earth elements to China
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is still considering an application to export rare earth carbonates to China, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup. He said Malaysia had previously exported rare earth carbonates to China but that shipments had since stopped while some exports to the United States had been approved. "We are still considering whether it will continue," he said when asked if exports to China would resume.

items.title: Mazda CX-5 grows up, putting family first
items.summary: THE third-generation Mazda CX-5 arrives with a bigger body, a more spacious cabin and a renewed focus on comfort. Now in its third generation, the CX-5 retains the familiar Mazda emphasis on driver engagement while addressing some of the predecessor's practical shortcomings, particularly rear passenger accommodation and luggage capacity. For Malaysian motorists who regularly travel between cities, navigate winding trunk roads or spend long hours on highways, these changes could make the latest model a more compelling family companion.

items.title: Rethinking EV motorsport: Grassroots autocross as Malaysia's high-tech incubator
items.summary: To the average Malaysian independent garage owner or paddock mechanic, these high-end racing series feel like science fiction - impressive to watch on television, but entirely irrelevant to their daily livelihood. If Malaysia is serious about upskilling its technical workforce for the electrified era, we need to start encouraging a new class of competitors: a separate hybrid class should be created for all levels of motorsport activities. With grassroots motorsports, we should focus on low-cost and accessible forms of racing - primarily Time Attack, Autocross, or Gymkhana.

items.title: NexG Bina's bank freeze lifted
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: NexG Bina Bhd says the freeze imposed on certain bank accounts maintained by the company and its subsidiaries with RHB Bank Bhd has been lifted by the relevant authorities. "The freezing imposed on certain bank accounts has been lifted by the relevant authorities," it said in a Bursa Malaysia filing. The company did not specify the number of bank accounts that had been unfrozen.

items.title: Anwar reflects on four years in office: More to be done for Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim reflected on his four years in office, acknowledging that much remains to be done to improve the lives of Malaysians. Anwar said deep-rooted weaknesses in governance and entrenched practices of corruption demanded bold action and reforms. Anwar said the government had, over the past four years, worked to strengthen the country's financial position, improve governance, push institutional reforms and reinforce public welfare.

items.title: Girl, 7, killed in four-vehicle crash on NSE near Kempas
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 7-year-old girl was killed after a Mercedes-Benz crashed into a Perodua Myvi, triggering a chain collision involving four vehicles on the North-South Expressway near Kempas. Johor Baru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrol Anuar Nor said preliminary investigations found that the Mercedes, driven by a 58-year-old man, had gone out of control before crashing into the rear of the Myvi. "The impact caused the Myvi to move forward and hit the rear of a Chery Tiggo, driven by a 72-year-old man, and a lorry driven by a 50-year-old man," he said in a statement today.

items.title: US blacklists Megaspeed, two Malaysian firms over AI chip diversion risk
items.summary: SINGAPORE: US authorities have barred Singapore-based tech group Megaspeed International from purchasing advanced chips in the fallout from an alleged Chinese espionage scandal surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. - INVESTIGATIONS - Megaspeed touts itself as a company at the heart of the artificial intelligence revolution, using Nvidia's advanced silicon chips to power high-performance computing inside vast data centres. - MSFUSION: MALAYSIA DATA CENTRE - Another company, MSFusion, was also added to the US blacklist.

items.title: Three Tangkak students to be charged tomorrow over bullying of schoolmate
items.summary: TANGKAK: Three male students will be charged in court tomorrow over the assault of a 14-year-old at a secondary school in the district. Deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Jamellulkamal Abdul Halim said the investigation papers were completed and referred to the state prosecution director's office. The victim was allegedly assaulted by three male students at 8am in the secondary school classroom on Nov 13, with a police report lodged the following day.

items.title: Berjaya Food to exit loss-making Kenny Rogers, retain 5pct stake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Food Bhd is restructuring its loss-making Kenny Rogers Roasters business in Malaysia by transferring its operations to a new joint venture (JV) company. Berjaya Food said it will retain a five per cent stake. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Berjaya Food said its wholly-owned subsidiary Berjaya Roasters (M) Sdn Bhd entered into a joint venture and shareholders' agreement with Samaya Food Investments LLC, Vertix Holdings LLC and Nabil Shaukat Butt on Nov 23.

items.title: Wrong car, not robbery attempt, says daughter of elderly 'robber'
items.summary: KEPALA BATAS: A viral video alleging an attempted robbery at a petrol station here stemmed from a misunderstanding, says the daughter of an elderly man accused of the act. Facebook user Siti Nur Nadieya claimed her father had mistaken another vehicle for the red Perodua Alza multi-purpose vehicle their family had rented for four days. He also assumed the woman refuelling the car was a petrol station attendant.

items.title: No more ‘white, round pills’: MySejahtera’s second life as Malaysia’s digital health hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — What began as a mandatory crisis response tool at the height of the Covid-19 pandemic has evolved into the cornerstone of Malaysia’s national digital health infrastructure, serving as a digital front door for millions of residents. Speaking to Malay Mail, Health Ministry Digital Health Division director Dr Maheshwara Rao Appannan said the MySejahtera application has successfully moved from contact tracing to a comprehensive public health platform, driving the ministry’s “One Person, One Record” vision. Dr Maheshwara said inclusivity was key to the strategy.

items.title: Otters make a splash in KL’s Klang River, bringing hope for cleaner waters — and trouble for fish pond owners
items.summary: Small groups of otters are now being seen regularly in parts of the city, including along the once heavily polluted Klang River. “Wherever there are otters, there are fish. So that’s one of the importance of otters,” he said.

items.title: Five minutes to Johor: Businesses hope new RTS Link with Singapore brings more than day-trippers
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 24 — If all goes according to plan, the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link will begin operations in February 2027, enhancing connectivity between Singapore and Malaysia, particularly Johor. With a capacity to carry approximately 40,000 passengers daily and train frequencies of six minutes during off-peak hours and 3.6 minutes during peak periods, the light rail transit shuttle service connecting Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru and Woodlands North in Singapore is expected to generate economic opportunities across various sectors in Johor. There is, however, another possibility: could the increased cross-border movement lead to Johor Bahru merely serving as a stopover, while the economic benefits are largely confined to businesses operating near the Bukit Chagar RTS station?

items.title: Teo: No licensing plan for online gaming firms as CMCF studies child safety risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The government has no plans to introduce special licensing requirements for online gaming service providers, unlike those implemented for social media platforms, says Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching. However, she said the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) is conducting a study to assess emerging risks and appropriate regulatory approaches for online gaming services. Teo said CMCF has held public consultations since September to develop a gaming subcode.

items.title: Even BN funded KLSCAH, Hannah Yeoh tells Parliament amid RM1,000 land premium row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Barisan Nasional administrations had previously given public funds to the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH), Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said today, as she pushed back against claims of preferential treatment over a nominal RM1,000 land premium granted to the heritage building. The DAP minister also sought to allay concerns over the status of Malay land in the federal capital, stressing that she had fought equally hard to preserve traditional Malay villages and Malay Reserve Land during her tenure. Yeoh said she had begun consultations with residents to formally zone traditional Malay enclaves, namely Kampung Sungai Penchala, Kampung Palimbayan and Kampung Bukit Lanjan, to preserve their heritage status.

items.title: Replica of Picasso work recovered from 1MDB to feature at KL art fair this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — A reproduction of a Pablo Picasso artwork linked to the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case will be featured in a special exhibition space at the Malaysia Art Ecosystem Fair (MAEF) 2026, to be held at the Kuala Lumpur World Trade Centre from Nov 27 to 29. National Art Gallery director-general Amerrudin Ahmad said the original work, titled L’Écuyère et Les Clowns, is a colour lithograph by Picasso dating back to 1961. Amerrudin said the exhibition space dedicated to the 1MDB-related artwork also aims to educate the public on integrity by highlighting the story behind the artwork.

items.title: Govt’s Duta Enclave valuation complied with law, Semantan Estate’s figure ‘excessively high’, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The High Court was told today that the Government’s valuation for acquiring 263.272 acres from Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 complied with the Land Acquisition Act and Malaysian Valuation Standards. Tan Tat Khuan, 40, assistant director of the Ministry of Finance’s Valuation and Property Services Department, testified that his valuation recommended compensation for land value only, unlike Semantan Estate’s claim, which covers both land value and compensation for severance and injurious affection (adverse effects from the acquisition). “The plaintiff’s valuer assessed the land at RM1.5 million; my valuation is RM875,000.

items.title: Nancy Shukri eyes homelessness Bill by 2028, says tackling foreign beggars needs inter-agency effort
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) aims to table a Bill specifically addressing homelessness by 2028 to tackle the issue more comprehensively and effectively. Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the drafting of the proposed legislation was still at an early stage, with the ministry currently undertaking an in-depth study on the matter. — Bernama

items.title: Anwar, Pakistan army chief Asim Munir discuss maritime security, counterterrorism cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Malaysia and Pakistan are committed to strengthening defence and security cooperation, including through trilateral cooperation with Türkiye, while exploring opportunities for collaboration in maritime security and counterterrorism efforts. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in a Facebook post today that the matters were discussed during a courtesy call by Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir. He said the meeting also provided an opportunity to exchange views on regional and international security developments, including efforts to ease tensions in West Asia and the importance of safeguarding global maritime security.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Pakatan pledges loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz, says crisis must not derail 2027 state budget
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 23 — Negeri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan (NSPH) hopes for an immediate resolution to the prolonged political and administrative crisis in the state to ensure the smooth functioning of the government and safeguard the interests of the people. “Negeri Sembilan has been gripped by political and administrative uncertainty for more than 100 days. “Negeri Sembilan should not continue to be a casualty of political manoeuvring by those entrusted with governing the state.

items.title: HRD Corp approves RM2.1b for worker training from this year’s levy collection, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The Human Resources Development Corporation (HRD Corp) collected RM2.223 billion in levies this year, of which RM2.099 billion, or 94.4 per cent, was approved as financial assistance to fund training programmes for local workers. He said HRD Corp used the levy collections to provide financing and training grants to employers to help improve workers’ skills through upskilling and reskilling programmes. Khairul Firdaus said HRD Corp also provided training grants in nine priority areas, including Industry 4.0, future technologies, fintech, blockchain and green technology, to ensure local workers remained relevant to current and future technological developments and industry requirements.

items.title: MAHB moves to fix KLIA VIP room after Sabah minister slips, hurts head
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 23 — Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) has initiated immediate rectification action following an incident in which a guest slipped and sustained a head injury at the Terminal 1 VIP Room of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) earlier today. In a statement today, the airport operator said KLIA regretted the incident and had addressed the feedback received from the affected guest. “KLIA regrets the incident that occurred in the Terminal 1 VIP Room earlier today and has addressed the feedback received from the affected guest.

items.title: Kangar police nab two suspected cable thieves after chase, gang leader among five on the run
items.summary: KANGAR, Nov 23 — Police have arrested two men believed to be members of the Mat Lan Keladi Gang, suspected of involvement in the theft of Telekom Malaysia ™ cables in front of Dataran Keris, Jalan Kangar-Alor Setar, here on Nov 17. Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the two men, aged 32 and 35, were arrested at 4.35 am following information from the public about a suspected cable theft at a petrol station in Taman Kemajuan here at 4.25 am. He said that upon arriving at the petrol station, police found three cars, with seven men believed to be involved in the cable theft.

items.title: ‘Stay calm, have confidence’: PM Anwar’s message to SPM 2026 candidates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today wished all candidates sitting for the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination success. “May everything go smoothly and may you be blessed with success, God willing,” he said. A total of 420,879 candidates have registered for the 2026 SPM examination at 3,334 examination centres nationwide, with the written papers scheduled from Nov 23 to Dec 17.

items.title: Zahid to attend Huffaz 26K 2026 gathering as 27 tahfiz institutions set for recognition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The Huffaz 26K 2026 gathering in Bagan Datuk, Perak, this Friday is expected to strengthen cooperation among tahfiz institutions and expand education and career opportunities for Quran memorisers. The Deputy Prime Minister’s Office said in a statement today that the gathering would bring together religious, academic and skills training institutions to strengthen the country’s tahfiz education ecosystem. Themed “Huffaz Memacu Peradaban” (Huffaz Driving Civilisation), the gathering will also focus on expanding technical and vocational education and training (TVET) pathways for tahfiz students.

items.title: No app, no personal data — Fahmi says MySiren alerts go straight to phones
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The National Early Warning System (MySiren), launched today, will function only by sending notifications to users, without having access to any personal data belonging to device owners. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the system, operated by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), uses Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology to deliver alerts directly to compatible mobile phones within designated geographical areas, without requiring users to install an application or register. Fahmi said a nationwide simultaneous test of MySiren’s alert reception system is scheduled for 10.10 am on Nov 29.

items.title: ‘Purpose not fulfilled’: Wong Soon Koh and grandson quit PDP, vow loyalty to GPS
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 23 — Bawang Assan incumbent assemblyman Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh and his grandson Sean Wong have resigned from the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP). Wong, who was PDP senior vice-president, formally tendered his resignation yesterday, giving up all party positions and appointments with immediate effect. On April 6, 2024, PDP president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing announced that Wong and two senior leaders of the now-dissolved Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) have taken up top positions in PDP.

items.title: Melaka govt accepts Khoo’s apology over Terengganu Friday closure remarks
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 23 — Muslim male workers in Melaka whose employers bar them from attending Friday prayers have been urged to report the matter to the authorities immediately so that action can be taken against those involved. State Religious Affairs, Entrepreneur Development, Cooperatives and Cost of Living Committee chairman Datuk Rais Yasin said preventing Muslim men from attending Friday prayers was inappropriate, as the prayers were an obligation for all Muslim men who had reached puberty, in Malaysia and abroad. He was responding to a question on whether Melaka would consider temporarily closing business premises to allow Muslim employees to attend Friday prayers, following a similar practice in Terengganu.

items.title: EC gazettes October electoral roll with 41,958 new voters, opens inspection until Jan 21
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 23 — A total of 41,958 Malaysians aged 18 and above were automatically registered as new voters in October, according to the Election Commission (EC). EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the registrations were included in the October 2026 Supplementary Electoral Roll (DPT BLN10/2026), which was gazetted today and is open for inspection for 60 days until Jan 21, 2027. He said the supplementary roll also recorded 17,076 registered voters who had changed their electoral constituencies and 4,109 who had changed their voter category or status.

items.title: Rubber tapper finds missing toddler safe after overnight search in Kuala Krai
items.summary: According to Sinar Harian (SH), Muhammad Irsyad Hakim Mohammad Khairul Najmi was found at about 10.20am in a hilly rubber plantation near Kampung Bechah Salak here. His father, Mohammad Khairul Najmi Mohd Rosli, 26, said he had barely slept since learning of his son’s disappearance, having rushed back from Bandar Jengka, Pahang, and joined the search effort through the night. Alhamdulillah, a rubber tapper found him safe.

items.title: Rumours of early Perak polls? Saarani says government still has a year
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 23 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said there are no plans or need to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly immediately after the tabling of the state’s Budget 2027 tomorrow. He said the decision to dissolve the state assembly falls under the prerogative powers of the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, and that reasonable grounds must be provided before submitting any request for dissolution. On Nov 18, the Perak Menteri Besar’s Office dismissed claims circulating on several social media platforms that Saarani had an audience with Sultan Nazrin Shah to seek, and had obtained, the Ruler’s consent to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.

items.title: Govt screens foreign workers with police checks, targets lower migrant workforce by 2030
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The government conducts background screenings of foreign workers through an integrated system with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to ensure they have no criminal records before being allowed into the country. Any foreign worker seeking employment must undergo the stipulated processes, which must be adhered to by employers intending to hire foreign workers. He said the foreign worker intake ceiling is expected to drop from 2.248 million in 2026 to 1.788 million in 2030, in line with the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).

items.title: After KLIA fall, Sabah minister urges better toilet safety and emergency access
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Sabah Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry Minister Datuk Jamawi Jaafar required stitches to his head after slipping on a toilet floor at the VIP lounge in the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) this morning. In a Facebook post, Jamawi said the incident occurred while he was using a toilet near Bilik Bunga Mawar in the airport’s VIP waiting area. “The slippery toilet floor caused me to slip and my head hit the floor,” he said.

items.title: ‘Why did he run away?’ Father of woman killed in Federal Highway crash demands answers
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 23 — The father of a 20-year-old woman killed in a Federal Highway crash has questioned why the Mercedes-Benz driver, who is still being sought by police, allegedly abandoned the scene instead of facing the consequences. The crash claimed the life of Tan Si Yin and another female passenger after both were thrown from the vehicle. If he was at fault, he should have taken responsibility,” Tan’s father told Berita Harian (BH) during her funeral today.

items.title: Cash offers and sponsored holidays: PAC flags ‘serious’ governance failures in UKM’s outsourced postgraduate programmes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia’s (UKM) previous administration sat on conflict-of-interest allegations for nearly eight months, while legal officers were said to have been offered cash and holiday sponsorships to fast-track contract reviews, Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) revealed today. The PAC also said it found attempts to conceal the names of officers holding key positions in Koperasi Siswazah Bangi Berhad (KSBB). Mas Ermieyati, MP for Masjid Tanah, said the PAC’s investigation found that even UKM’s Internal Investigation Committee (JKSD) initially suffered from structural conflicts of interest.

items.title: Selangor sets aside RM3m for free meals for 73,594 SPM candidates
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 23 — The Selangor government has allocated RM3 million to provide free meals to 73,594 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates across the state under the Selangor Nutrition (NutriSel) SPM 2026 initiative. He said a total of 71,152 SPM candidates from 256 schools would benefit from the initiative, covering Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK), Sekolah Agama Menengah (SAM), Sekolah Agama Menengah Tinggi (SAMT), Sekolah Menengah Persendirian Cina (SMPC), special model schools and private tahfiz schools. “Another 2,442 SPM candidates from 20 schools or institutions will also benefit.

items.title: Johor sets aside RM5m to spruce up Larkin Sentral by Christmas after MB’s surprise visit
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 23 — The Johor government has allocated RM5 million for maintenance and improvement works on facilities at the Larkin Sentral Public Transport Terminal in Johor Bahru. State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said the works will be carried out in phases as a short-term effort to upgrade the facilities. “The identified repair works include the maintenance of infrastructure and public amenities, as well as improvements to cleanliness and passenger comfort.

items.title: Cable theft leaves 450 street lights in Putrajaya out of service, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Underground cable theft has been identified as the cause of 450 street lights along federal roads FT29 and FT30 in Putrajaya being out of service, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan. “Each solar-powered street light costs RM10,000, while conventional street lights cost between RM4,000 and RM5,000 each. Conventional street lights are vulnerable to cable theft, while solar-powered street lights come with a five-year warranty compared with two years for conventional street lights.

items.title: Pahang open to data centres, but only in Gambang and Gebeng
items.summary: KUANTAN, Nov 23 — Gambang and Gebeng here have been identified as the two locations with sufficient infrastructure, including land, water and electricity supply, as well as fibre optic connectivity, to support data centre development in Pahang. Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Nizar Najib said the state government would, however, closely scrutinise and monitor all data centre developments to ensure they did not affect electricity and water supplies for residents. Mohamad Nizar said applications for data centre development at the Federal Government level were currently facing lengthy waiting periods, with new projects expected to materialise only within the next one to two years.

items.title: Johor sets aside RM3.8m to keep free medicine delivery service running in 2027
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 23 — The Johor state government has allocated RM3.8 million to continue the free Medicine by Post (UMP) initiative for all Johoreans next year, said State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon. He said the allocation will benefit approximately 35,000 patients, with a target of serving 1,000 patients per month. He noted that the state government began covering the costs of the UMP service on August 1, 2024.
